record.original_question: Let n1, n2, n3 be pairwise relatively prime positive integers, and let u be a positive integer with u n2 == 1 mod n1. Find a formula, in terms of n1, n2, n3, for the multiplicity of the proportionally modular numerical semigroup S(u n2 n3, n1 n2, n3), equivalently for the invariant c3 needed to recover the Frobenius problem in embedding dimension 3.

evidence.quote: Therefore, if we had a formula for computing c3 from n1 and n2, we would have solved the problems raised by Frobenius for embedding dimension three.
We suggest in this line the problem of finding a formula that allows us to give the multiplicity of S(un2 n3, n1 n2, n3) from n1, n2 and n3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A proportionally modular numerical semigroup is a set of the form
S(a,b,c) = { x ∈ ℕ : a x mod b ≤ c x },
where a, b, c are positive integers and ℕ = {0,1,2,…}; this set is a numerical semigroup (a cofinite submonoid of ℕ).

The multiplicity of a numerical semigroup S, denoted m(S), is the smallest positive integer that belongs to S.

Let n₁, n₂, n₃ be pairwise relatively prime positive integers, and let u be a positive integer such that u n₂ ≡ 1 (mod n₁). Consider the proportionally modular numerical semigroup
S = S(u n₂ n₃, n₁ n₂, n₃) = { x ∈ ℕ : (u n₂ n₃) x mod (n₁ n₂) ≤ n₃ x }.

Problem: Find a closed-form formula, expressed only in terms of n₁, n₂, n₃ (and depending on u only through these data), for the multiplicity m(S) of S.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as open in the numerical semigroups problem list and is connected to the unsolved Frobenius problem in embedding dimension three. No subsequent paper found in the search provides a closed-form formula for the multiplicity of S(un₂n₃, n₁n₂, n₃) in terms of n₁, n₂, n₃; standard surveys still report no general formula for the Frobenius number (or related invariants) in embedding dimension ≥ 3.

status_evidence.title: Numerical semigroups problem list
status_evidence.snippet: We suggest in this line the problem of finding a formula that allows us to give the multiplicity of S(un2 n3, n1 n2, n3) from n1, n2 and n3.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: The Frobenius problem for numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: There is no known general formula to compute the Frobenius number of numerical semigroups having embedding dimension three or more.
status_evidence.claim: No general formula in embedding dimension three is known, supporting the open status.
